To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified two low-energy conformers of the amino group in the equatorial position with respect to the indan ring in the chiral (S)-1-amino-indan molecule and that we studied the vibrational spectra and the formation of complexes with methyllactate in a supersonic expansion.

two conformers of chiral ( R )-1-aminoindane were identified in supersonic jets by laser-induced fluorescence and single vibrational level emission spectroscopy and the ground state frequencies of their low-frequency ring puckering modes were determined.
the aminoindan molecule has been found to exist as two conformers, which form complexes with water, methyllactate and methanol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spectroscopy of the aminoindan molecule and some of its complexes in supersonic jet, and the influence of chirality on the formation of these complexes.
the spectroscopic properties of chiral molecules and their complexes.
chiral molecules, which are of interest to the chemical industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two conformers are not distinguishable in the free state, but their complexation with methyllactate and water is selective and can be used for their separation.
the two chiral conformers of (R)-1-AID have been identified and their ground and first excited states vibrational spectra have been investigated by LIF, SVL, and theoretical methods.
the aminoindan molecule is chiral and the amino group is directed to the opposite side of the aromatic ring in the two lowest energy conformers, which is in agreement with the ab initio calculations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chiral amino group is not the main factor for the formation of these clusters.
chiral aminoindan molecules are able to distinguish between enantiomers of methyllactate in the supersonic jet.

the amino group in the two lowest-energy conformers of (R)-1-aminindan molecule is in the equatorial position with the lone pair directed away from the aromatic ring, and the two lowest-energy modes are the puckering motion and the ring flapping motion, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amino group in (R)-1-AI is in the equatorial position, with its lone pair oriented opposite to the aromatic ring.

the chiral (S)/(R)-1-aminoisobenzene molecule, whose two lowest-energy structures have also been identified in supersonic expansion, forms similar 1 :1 water clusters with the same 0-0 transition blue-shift, while its complexes with (S)/(R) -methyllactate are different, with different blue-shifts and different SVL spectra.

chiral molecules may be able to distinguish between chiral and achiral molecules in the environment, even in the case when the interaction between the chiral and achiral molecules is weak and the energy of the complexes is similar to the energy of the isolated molecules.
